clue.text: Son, unfriendly in front of editor, gets told off

indicators.note: says the preceding pieces come before the editor's letters

parts.note: an unfriendly manner is a cold one

explanation.surface: A boy who is frosty towards his newspaper boss gets a dressing-down.
explanation.definitionFit: To be told off is to be reprimanded, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Cons — and those who guard them

definitions.meaning: to con someone is to cheat or swindle them
prison officers, called ... in British slang, guard convicts (cons)

explanation.surface: Prisoners and their warders are mentioned together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cons' reads as a noun (convicts), which sets up the warders, but as the first definition it is a verb meaning cheats.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses the same word both for swindles as a verb and for prison warders as a noun.

clue.text: Nothing to cook in base

parts.note: the letter O looks like zero, nothing
to cook the books is to rig or falsify them

explanation.surface: Nothing to cook at home base — an empty larder.
explanation.definitionFit: A base is a starting point or source, which is what an origin is.

clue.text: Regularly find rising juice before fruit goes off

indicators.note: says the juice comes ahead of the fruit
in a down clue, rising means the picked letters are read upwards, backwards
taking every other letter of the word find, its second and fourth

parts.note: sap is the juice of a plant
pears are a fruit

explanation.surface: A recipe step: find some juice, then the fruit spoils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' picks ID from 'find', and 'rising' turns it to DI.
explanation.definitionFit: To go off can mean to leave or vanish from sight, a synonym for vanishing.

clue.text: More withered veterans initially dropped off by motorist

indicators.note: the veterans' letter is shed by the motorist's word, as a passenger is set down

parts.note: a motorist is a driver

indicators.note: takes just the opening letter of veterans

explanation.surface: Elderly old soldiers are given a lift and dropped off by a driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Something more withered is more parched and dried out, the comparative of a dry thing.

clue.text: Credit cards snap around end

indicators.note: the photo's letters go around the other word

parts.note: a snap is a photograph, PIC for short
to last is to endure, to go on to the end

explanation.surface: Credit cards snapping around the edges — worn out from use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' is a verb here: to last.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment cards are informally called by the name of the material they are made from.

clue.text: Budding plant's container — lean it precariously

parts.note: a plant is kept in a pot

indicators.note: something placed precariously is unsteady, so these letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A potted plant's container is perched at a risky angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A budding talent is one that is promising but not yet realised, that is, latent.

clue.text: Powerless couples displaying affectation of superiority

indicators.note: the word for couples is left without its P, the abbreviation for power

parts.note: couples are pairs

explanation.surface: Couples with no clout put on a show of superiority anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the physics abbreviation for power.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on airs is an idiom for behaving as though better than others.

clue.text: Time to misbehave with current female? One Conservative's wicked

parts.note: to err is to stray or do wrong
I is the symbol for electric current
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A tale of an affair: a Tory is accused of being wicked for straying with a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' looks like moral condemnation but is slang praise.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, wicked means excellent, which is what this word means informally.

clue.text: Seizing animal by lower jaw and tail in building

parts.note: a cat is an animal
the chin is the front of the lower jaw

indicators.note: takes the final letter of building, its tail

explanation.surface: A predator grabs a cat by its jaw and tail inside a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Seizing something is grabbing hold of it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Spoils game in seconds

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A game is ruined in a matter of seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil something is to wreck it, the verb sense.

clue.text: Half interested, ready for Macron to explain

indicators.note: takes the first five of the ten letters of interested

parts.note: French President Macron would say 'prêt' for ready

explanation.surface: Someone half-engaged is ready to explain things to the French president.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain the meaning of something is to elucidate it, a synonym.

clue.text: Wife exercises with hoop after the man's muttering

indicators.note: the exercises and hoop come after the man's word

parts.note: his means belonging to the man
PE is physical education, exercises at school
a hoop is a ring

explanation.surface: A wife works out with a hula hoop while her husband grumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Muttering is speaking softly under the breath, a near synonym.

clue.text: Person who's smashing plate

definitions.meaning: an attractive, gorgeous person is informally called this
a plate or serving vessel for food

explanation.surface: Someone is breaking crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' suggests breaking the plate, but it means attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a good-looking person in slang and a serving vessel.

clue.text: People on buses perhaps see prangs developing and start to shout

indicators.note: as events develop, these letters change into a new form
takes the first letter of shout

explanation.surface: Bus riders watch a crash unfold and begin to yell.
explanation.walkthrough: A prang is British slang for a minor car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders on any vehicle are its travellers; buses are one example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Engineer repairs tip — no sweat

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rework, so these letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: An engineer finds repairing the end easy: no sweat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no sweat' reads as an idiom for easy, but 'no' is fodder and 'sweat' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweat and its formal word for bodily moisture are direct synonyms.

clue.text: Training fish to follow reduced group of whales

indicators.note: the fish comes after the shortened group
the word for the group is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a school is a group of whales, dolphins or fish
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Teaching a fish to swim behind a small pod of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: Training and education are both instruction, a synonym.

clue.text: Broken nails, say, producing criticism

indicators.note: the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A manicurist's critique of chipped fingernails.
explanation.definitionFit: Critical examination of a work, as in literary criticism, is a close study of it.

clue.text: I have sent over study by the Church for authentication

indicators.note: turned over, so the contraction is read backwards

parts.note: contracts to I've
a den is a study or private room
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone has posted their study notes to the Church for verification.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof that establishes something as genuine is what authentication requires.

clue.text: In spite of everything, neither vessel at sea ignores island

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the letters are in disorder
one letter is left out of the jumbled pool

explanation.surface: Despite everything, neither ship at sea calls at the island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' mixes NEITHER VESSEL, and 'ignores' drops its I (island) from the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase in spite of everything means notwithstanding, a synonym of this adverb.

clue.text: Voice quality encapsulates good, upper-class dialect

indicators.note: the voice-quality word wraps around the next two letters

parts.note: a voice's tone is its quality
U denotes upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A posh accent's vocal quality is described.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue is a language or way of speaking, close to a regional variety.

clue.text: Snake European caught with tense appearance

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A snake is caught on the Continent, looking nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: The look or outward appearance of something is its facet as seen.

clue.text: Pool game with international appearing for university

indicators.note: the international letter stands in for the university one

parts.note: ludo is a board game

explanation.surface: Pool is a game that an international player represents his university in.
explanation.walkthrough: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor public swimming pool is called by this Italian-derived name.

clue.text: Old politician in jail is gathering acceptable friends

indicators.note: the old politician's letters go inside the jail

parts.note: the can is slang for jail
an MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: the word is collects the acceptable letters inside it

parts.note: something 'on' is acceptable, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: A jailed former MP is making respectable friends inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Friends are mates, people who keep one company.

clue.text: Rubbish boxers?

definitions.meaning: British slang for worthless or poor
boxer shorts are men's underwear, and the question mark flags the example

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on some fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxers' suggests fighters, but it means boxer shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for nonsense and also means underwear, of which boxers are one kind.

clue.text: Artist somewhat weird? A little

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The artist is described as a bit odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador of Spain was a Surrealist painter famed for melting clocks.

clue.text: Scandal in Eton as unruly head of science is imprisoned

indicators.note: the science letter is locked inside the jumbled letters
unruly letters are disorderly, so they are rearranged
takes the first letter of science

explanation.surface: A scandal at Eton school as an unruly head of science is jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' rearranges IN ETON AS, and S is placed inside. Eton is a famous English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal causes a stir or furore, the newspaper sense of a sensational story.

clue.text: Almost keen to capture large bird

indicators.note: the shortened word surrounds the large letter
the word for keen is shortened by its final letter

parts.note: keen means eager

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher is nearly eager enough to catch a big bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bird of prey is the example here.

clue.text: Looking for Neptune, we hear?

indicators.note: says the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: Neptune is the Roman god of the sea, a sea king

explanation.surface: A question: is someone searching for the sea god?
explanation.definitionFit: Looking for something is searching or hunting for it.

clue.text: Presume American quietly gets ensnared by cult

indicators.note: the American and quiet letters are trapped inside the cult

parts.note: a sect is a cult
P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: An American drawn quietly into a cult — a familiar news story.
explanation.definitionFit: To presume something is to suppose or guess it is so.
